issuesMerged.problem: The XOR plate shows THAT the rule fails, never WHAT was shown or WHY. The main try boxes carry a glyph of each shape (— ✕, | ✕), but the XOR try boxes carry only ✓ and ✗. A 15-year-old cannot tell which of the four cases (neither, top, bottom, both) each try was. The plate also never says 'one layer'. Claim limit-linear's caveat is that the limit belongs to the single-layer machine, and the Mark I itself had a random association layer. As it stands, an expert can read 'It could learn only simple patterns … XOR never settles' as a claim about the whole Mark I and about neural networks in general.
issuesMerged.fix: Keep the real trainXor() run. (1) Give each XOR try box a tiny two-dot glyph of its case (○○ ●○ ○● ●●) before its ✓ or ✗, matching the main row's style. (2) Under the 'XOR · one lit, not both' caption, add a second line in the same face: 'one layer of dials'. (3) Optional depth beat, only if it is true in the actual run: the first time the run gets the both-lit case wrong, show the two lit dials' tugs adding past the threshold tick (two small arc arrows stacking), so the viewer sees why. Two tugs that each say yes say yes together. This is the linear-separability intuition with no algebra. Hold to the existing beats; no narration change (runtime is 67.75 s against the 68 s cap).

Add a clear 'years' dim with '→ the 1970s'.
